questions.question: If 21 March 2007 is a Wednesday, what would be the day of the week on 25 May 2015?
questions.solution:
We know that:

In an ordinary year, there are 365 days and by dividing 365 by 7,

 
• We get remainder = 1 so this extra **one day** is taken as an odd day.

Similarly, in a leap year, there are 366 days and on dividing 366 by 7,

 
• we get remainder = 2 so these extra **two days** are taken as odd days.

**Thus, the remainder, which we get after dividing the number of days by 7 is considered odd days.**

Given 21 March 2007 is a Wednesday.

Since 2007 is a non-leap year.

 
• **Number of odd days from the year 2007 to the year 2015 = (1 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1) = 10**

Number of odd days from 2007 to 2015 = 10 ÷ 7 = 3 odd days

∴ On 21 March 2015,** it was Wednesday + 3 = Saturday**

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of deforestation?

options.text: Decrease in level of ground water
Increase in pollution level on earth
Increase in level of oxygen in the atmosphere
Disturbance in the overall balance of nature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in level of oxygen in the atmosphere.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An increase in the level of oxygen in the atmosphere** is not a consequence of deforestation.
 
• Deforestation is a very broad term, which consists of cutting of trees including repeated lopping, felling, and removal of forest litter, browsing, grazing, and trampling of seedlings.
 
• **Consequences of Deforestation:-**
 
• Loss of Habitat
 
 
• 70% of land animals and plant species live in forests. 
 
• **Disturbance in the overall balance of nature.**
 
• The trees of the rainforest that provide shelter for some species also provide the canopy that regulates the temperature.
 
• Deforestation results in a more drastic temperature variation from day to night, much like a desert, which could prove fatal for many inhabitants. 
 
 
 
• Soil Erosion
 
 
• Trees help the land retain water and topsoil, which provides the rich nutrients to sustain additional forest life.
 
• Without forests, the soil erodes and washes away, causing farmers to move on and perpetuate the cycle.
 
 
 
• Desertification
 
 
• It is a transformation of once fertile land into a desert.
 
• **Decrease in level of groundwater.**
 
• It refers to the persistent degradation of dryland ecosystems by climatic variations and human activities.
 
• If trees are removed, the area can become much warmer and drier, which may result in desertification.
 
 
 
• Climate Change
 
 
• Trees and other plants absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere as they grow.
 
• **Increase in pollution level on earth.**
 
• This is converted into carbon and stored in the plant’s branches, leaves, trunks, roots, and soil.
 
• When forests are cleared or burnt, the stored carbon is released into the atmosphere, mainly as carbon dioxide.
 
• This leads to climate change.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Causes of Deforestation: The most common reason for deforestation is the cutting of wood for fuel, lumber, and paper. Another important cause relates to the clearing of forest land for agriculture, including conversion to cropland and pasture. The main causes of deforestation are:

 
 
• Agriculture
 
• Shifting cultivation
 
• Demand for firewood
 
• Wood for industry and commercial use
 
• Urbanization and developmental projects
 
• Overgrazing of forests

questions.question: As per the Census of India–2011, there are ______ statutory towns in the country

__
 
• A **Statutory Town** is one with a municipality, corporation, cantonment board, or notified town area committee.

 
 
• As per the 2011 Census, there are **4,041 such towns as against 3,799 in 2001.**
 
 
 
• A census town is one which is not statutorily notified and administered as a town, but whose population has attained urban characteristics.
 
 
• As per the 2011 Census, there are **3,784 Census Towns against 1,362 in 2001.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• A Census Town is an area with urban characteristics like

 
 
• A minimum population of 5,000
 
• At least 75% of the male main working force engaged in non-agricultural activities
 
• Population density of at least 400 persons per km2
